figures.llm_description: Figure 1. Ordering of the magnetic dipoles in magnetic materials.

figures.title: Figure 10
figures.llm_description: Figure 10. Comparison of ab initio ∆1 bands with those obtained from a tight-binding fit using only Mn and O orbitals in the basis. The fit for LaMnO3 is good, indicating that only the Mn and O ions are significantly involved in covalent bonding. The fit for BiMnO3 has a higher RMS deviation and, in particular, misses the additional curvature at around -3 eV near the X point. This shows that additional interactions are present.

figures.title: Figure 11
figures.llm_description: Figure 11. Comparison of ab initio ∆1 bands with those obtained from a tight-binding fit including Bi 6s and 6p orbitals in addition to Mn 3d and O 2s and 2p. The fit is improved over the fit using only Mn and O orbitals.

figures.title: Figure 14
figures.llm_description: Figure 14. (a) Eigenvector of the unstable ferroelectric Γ point phonon mode in BiMnO3. The Mn ion is at the center of the unit cell surrounded by an octahedra of oxygens, with the large cations at the unit cell corners. (b) Nonferroelectric mode that is unstable in LaMnO3. Each mode is 3-fold degenerate.

figures.title: Figure 15
figures.llm_description: Figure 15. Hexagonal perovskite structure. The small B cation (in black) is 5-fold-coordinated by oxygen anions (in gray). The dashed lines indicate the oxygen pentahedra. The large A cations (white) occupy 7-fold-coordinated sites.
